pr_title: sql: avoid stampede on synthetic privilege cache in vtable population
pr_body:
Accessing the synthetic privilege cache requires fetching the descriptor
for system.system_privileges, even in the case of a cache hit. This is
ok for the basic case of fetching a single privilege descriptor for one
virtual table, which is done when executing something like `SELECT *
FROM a_virtual_table`.

However, for some virtual tables, like pg_class, populating the table
itself requires fetching a privilege descriptor for each row in the result.
If a query does a lot of joins, that can mean hundreds of thousands of
calls to the synthetic privilege cache and the descriptor catalog. This
leads to a lot of thrashing in the descriptor catalog, since the catalog
is also being upserted into at the same time, since populating virtual
tables also requires fetching many descriptors.

This can be avoided by some small code changes that short-circuit and
avoid hitting the synthetic privilege cache entirely.

Before:
```
BenchmarkORMQueries/prisma_column_descriptions-10         	       1	6824922583 ns/op
```
After:
```
BenchmarkORMQueries/prisma_column_descriptions-10         	       1	2601088125 ns/op
```

fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/108781

Release note (performance improvement): Queries that access the
pg_catalog and information_schema that perform introspection on other
tables in those schemas are now signicantly faster.

Release note (sql change): Introspection queries will now show the
internal `node` user as the owner of tables in pg_catalog and
information_schema. Previously the owner was shown as `admin`, but that
was inaccurate since users with the `admin` role could not modify these
tables in any way.

issue_context.title: A SQL query used for introspecting a large database schema got 200x slower
issue_context.body: **Describe the problem** Prisma has an introspecting feature that looks at a database and creates a Prisma schema out of it, it is called `prisma db pull` One of the introspection SQL query is now very slow, 500s+ for `discourse` which has 140 tables (see link in To Reproduce). I do not know exactly at the moment for which version it started, my best guest is v23.1.x **To Reproduce** What did you do? Describe in your own words. If possible, provide steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Set up a serverless CockroachDB cluster in the Cloud UI 2. Use https://github.com/prisma/database-schema-examples/blob/main/postgres/discourse/schema.sql to create a database 3. Run the following SQL query on that database ```sql SELECT oid.namespace, info.table_name, info.column_name, format_type(att.atttypid, att.atttypmod) AS formatted_type, info.numeric_precision, info.numeric_scale, info.numeric_precision_radix, info.datetime_precision, info.data_type, info.udt_schema AS type_schema_name, info.udt_name AS full_data_type, pg_get_expr(attdef.adbin, attdef.adrelid) AS column_default, info.is_nullable, info.is_identity, info.character_maximum_length, description.description FROM information_schema.columns AS info JOIN pg_attribute AS att ON att.attname = info.column_name JOIN ( SELECT pg_class.oid, relname, pg_namespace.nspname AS namespace FROM pg_class JOIN pg_namespace ON pg_namespace.oid = pg_class.relnamespace AND pg_namespace.nspname = ANY (ARRAY['public']) ) AS oid ON oid.oid = att.attrelid AND relname = info.table_name AND namespace = info.table_schema LEFT JOIN pg_attrdef AS attdef ON attdef.adrelid = att.attrelid AND attdef.adnum = att.attnum AND table_schema = namespace LEFT JOIN pg_description AS description ON description.objoid = att.attrelid AND description.objsubid = ordinal_position WHERE table_schema = ANY (ARRAY['public']) AND info.is_hidden = 'NO' ORDER BY namespace, table_name, ordinal_position ``` 5. Wait for 500~ seconds for it to complete 6. Note that removing this part of the query `table_schema = ANY (ARRAY['public']) AND` and running it again makes it succeed in 2s. **Expected behavior** It should be (a lot?) faster to execute. **Additional data / screenshots** Diagnostic archive from the Cloud UI, from https://cockroachlabs.cloud/cluster/6fcad804-83d9-4f9b-b80b-b5b7b789a93c/statement/true/11919201472824938241?appNames=%28unset%29&cluster-type=serverless&tab=overview : [stmt-bundle-890298509353746433.zip](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/files/12346113/stmt-bundle-890298509353746433.zip) **Environment:** - CockroachDB version: v23.1.8 - cockroachlabs.cloud / Serverless - Server OS: Linux - Ubuntu - GitHub Actions - Client app: Prisma Client **Additional context** The CockroachDB server is https://cockroachlabs.cloud/cluster/6fcad804-83d9-4f9b-b80b-b5b7b789a93c/overview?cluster-type=serverless It's only used for tests, feel free to take a look, there is no data, only schemas we gathered for running tests. Shared in our shared [Slack channel](https://prisma-company.slack.com/archives/C01CSQXTNJ3/p1691768436839419) Jira issue: CRDB-30636 Epic CRDB-27601

Thanks for this report. I'll leave notes here as I discover things -- this is the slow part from the statement bundle:
```
            └── • virtual table lookup join
                │ nodes: n1
                │ actual row count: 1,286
                │ sql cpu time: 14m43s
                │ table: pg_namespace@pg_namespace_oid_idx
                │ equality: (relnamespace) = (oid)
                │ pred: (nspname = table_schema) AND (nspname = 'public')
```

Here's a simple reproduction: https://gist.github.com/mgartner/ec703b77e224297b75bf18f42420b266 The CPU profile (here: [discourse.cpu.zip](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/files/12432791/discourse.cpu.zip)) shows that most of the time is spent fetching all the descriptors for each lookup of the virtual table lookup join: This query got slower in v23.1 because the `pg_namespace@pg_namespace_oid_idx` was added. The optimizer now selects a plan that performs lookup joins with that index. #55833 was supposed to reduce the likelihood of selecting plans with virtual table lookup joins. It's possible that the fixed cost added for each lookup doesn't sufficiently represent the real cost of each lookup, which seems to scale as a function of the number of descriptors. I'll continue to investigate why the optimizer is picking this plan.

I no longer believe the optimizer is to blame here. The execution of this query appears to be way slower that it should be.

It seems like there's some issue when iterating over descriptors in the lookup join while also iterating over descriptors in the virtual scan that causes execution to grind to a halt. Pinging @cockroachdb/sql-foundations incase y'all have any ideas.

I have three somewhat unrelated points. See below.

---

Thanks to @mgartner's profile, I realized that the problem is with `syntheticprivilegecache.(*Cache).Get`. 

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/87fc44f15e40c8e3af5207e73955f42c278c0b2b/pkg/sql/syntheticprivilegecache/cache.go#L71-L77

This is called whenever we need to access privileges for virtual tables - which is something we need to do when populating `pg_class`. The issue is that each call to the cache includes that call to `descs.PrefixAndTable` in order to get the descriptor version for the internal `system.system_privileges` table.

That's fine when doing a one-off privilege check, like what would happen for a `SELECT * from pg_roles`. But it becomes much more problematic when it is called once for each of the thousands of rows in the result of the query in the initial issue report.

Luckily, we can actually avoid accessing the synthetic privilege cache with this change:
```
diff --git a/pkg/sql/authorization.go b/pkg/sql/authorization.go
index 22bff759daa..24c3a0729d9 100644
--- a/pkg/sql/authorization.go
+++ b/pkg/sql/authorization.go
@@ -363,6 +363,9 @@ func (p *planner) CheckGrantOptionsForUser(
 func (p *planner) getOwnerOfPrivilegeObject(
 	ctx context.Context, privilegeObject privilege.Object,
 ) (username.SQLUsername, error) {
+	if d, ok := privilegeObject.(catalog.TableDescriptor); ok && d.IsVirtualTable() {
+		return username.NodeUserName(), nil
+	}
 	privDesc, err := p.getPrivilegeDescriptor(ctx, privilegeObject)
 	if err != nil {
 		return username.SQLUsername{}, err
diff --git a/pkg/sql/information_schema.go b/pkg/sql/information_schema.go
index 7e8e7f1973c..444a6282870 100644
--- a/pkg/sql/information_schema.go
+++ b/pkg/sql/information_schema.go
@@ -2931,26 +2931,23 @@ func userCanSeeDescriptor(
 		return false, nil
 	}
 
+	// Users can see objects in the database if they have connect privilege.
+	if parentDBDesc != nil {
+		if ok, err := p.HasPrivilege(ctx, parentDBDesc, privilege.CONNECT, p.User()); err != nil {
+			return false, err
+		} else if ok {
+			return true, nil
+		}
+	}
 	// TODO(richardjcai): We may possibly want to remove the ability to view
 	// the descriptor if they have any privilege on the descriptor and only
 	// allow the descriptor to be viewed if they have CONNECT on the DB. #59827.
-	canSeeDescriptor := false
 	if ok, err := p.HasAnyPrivilege(ctx, desc); err != nil {
 		return false, err
-	} else {
-		canSeeDescriptor = ok
-	}
-	// Users can see objects in the database if they have connect privilege.
-	if parentDBDesc != nil {
-		if !canSeeDescriptor {
-			if ok, err := p.HasPrivilege(ctx, parentDBDesc, privilege.CONNECT, p.User()); err != nil {
-				return false, err
-			} else {
-				canSeeDescriptor = ok
-			}
-		}
+	} else if ok {
+		return true, nil
 	}
-	return canSeeDescriptor, nil
+	return false, nil
 }
 
 func descriptorIsVisible(desc catalog.Descriptor, allowAdding bool) bool {
```

With these two changes, the latency goes back down to 117ms when I tried locally. (It was several minutes locally before.)

---

I think the example in https://gist.github.com/mgartner/4f01c3d61898e015bd2487e34b68edab is different than the original issue.

- It takes 6.197s on 23.1.8
- It takes 7.442s on 22.2.8 (so this is not a 23.1 regression)
- My patch above makes it take 5.020s (so the cause of the slowness is clearly different)

---

Time: 190.152s total (execution 190.151s / network 0.001s)

So this is also some other (possibly a third) issue.

I have created the PR for the above (https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/109517). It still does seem potentially worthwhile to figure out if the lookup join to `pg_namespace` could be avoided though. I think that would reduce latency even further, since there would be fewer descriptor lookups. Any thoughts on that @mgartner ?

I believe the issue is that we don't collect statistics on virtual tables, so the optimizer makes some incorrect assumptions about how many rows will be produced at each step of the query plan. This causes the optimizer to choose a bad plan. Work to improve this is tracked by https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/27611.

review_comments: Can be simplified to `return ok, nil`.
i like doing it this way since if the code is copy-pasted, or if something else is added after this line, it's less likely for something to be forgotten.
